phase: wolfrpg modern default-mode fixtures (default table indices 6, 7, 8)

vendor.table: WolfDec::DefaultCryptModes(), added by build/vcpkg/ports/uberwolf/default-crypt-modes.patch over the unchanged DEFAULT_CRYPT_MODES table

generator.comparison: every produced path and byte compared against the owned input tree; the oracle was required to PASS before freezing each container
generator.timestamp_policy: the two input files and the nested directory are stamped to a fixed FILETIME; the encoder is driven with a relative "." root so the top-level directory's live access time is never recorded
generator.determinism_note: the pinned encoder is not byte-reproducible across runs: even with identical stamped inputs the archive size and the compressed table region vary, so the frozen container bytes and their sha256 are authoritative
generator.payload_note: sub/repeat.bin keeps a genuine repeat but uses a 2048-byte owned block so the container clears the pinned v3.31/v3.50 encoder+decoder floor (they early-return when body < 0x400 bytes); a smaller container silently produced no output and that failure is recorded, not masked

payloads.generator: literal "Owned WolfRPG fixture payload" plus a trailing LF
payloads.source: DARC_FILEHEAD HuffPressDataSize read from the exact frozen containers; the body is Huffman-only pressed (no LZ) so it expands 30 -> 252 bytes

payloads.generator: a 2048-byte xorshift32(0x51ED2701) owned block repeated four times
payloads.source: DARC_FILEHEAD PressDataSize/HuffPressDataSize read from the exact frozen containers; stored_size is the HuffPressDataSize the reader reports

oracle.tool: out/scratch/wolfrpg-default/probe.cpp (untracked scratch); drives the unchanged pinned vendor decoder DXArchive::DecodeArchive, the decFunc of the default table entry, on a read-only copy of each frozen container
oracle.metadata: the per-entry DataSize/PressDataSize/HuffPressDataSize above were read back from the exact frozen containers by replaying the pinned decoder's header step with the pinned crypt primitives and then walking the typed DARC_HEAD/DARC_FILEHEAD/DARC_DIRECTORY records; the recovered paths (hello.txt, sub/repeat.bin) and DataSize values (30, 8192) confirm the parse
oracle.decode_correct_key: all three containers decode rc=0; hello.txt and sub/repeat.bin both MATCH the owned plaintext (fnv1a64 hello 45cb0322a9a90780, repeat dae3c866244a0505)
oracle.decode_wrong_key_v331: cryptVersion 331 does not accept a wrong password: the pinned decoder faults (0xc0000374) instead of returning the payloads, so the reader contract is to reject
oracle.decode_wrong_key_v350_chacha100: cryptVersion 350 and 100 return the exact same payload bytes under the wrong password "not-the-default-key" (both MATCH), because v3.50 salts with the fixed literal "958" and default ChaCha2 keeps a fixed key/nonce
oracle.no_regeneration: the 3137-byte containers are authoritative; a later re-run of the scratch encoder produced 3158/3159-byte variants for modes 6/7 and those were never used as the expected source

test_bug_corrections: stored_size: the unit test asserted stored_size == plaintext size; the physically stored extent is 252 and 2402 bytes, so the expectation now uses the frozen encoded extent while unpacked_size stays 30 and 8192

password: the unit test asserted a wrong password is always rejected; v3.50 and default ChaCha2 ignore the password string, so those two modes now assert password invariance (open/list/extract the exact frozen bytes) and only v3.31 keeps the negative rejection.
expected_state: RED until integration: the current reader slice implements only the uncompressed DX8 container and rejects keyed/head-pressed headers with read_error, so the positive sections fail while the v3.31 negative control passes for the wrong reason. GREEN requires the modern modes in the reused backend.
